1. (25 points) Using data from college football seasons 2022 to 2025, filter to the games that are only FBS v FBS and make the plots from the Expected Points notebook from class using that data.

2. (25 points)  In class we talked about the 3rd and X model.  Using data from the most recent 5 NFL seasons, fit the model described in class and in a well written paragraph evaluate the claim that ``all teams in the NFL are equally good at making 3rd and X.''  Explain any choices that you made regarding the data and the models.

-------------------------------------------------
Graph bin limits were increased to 400 due to dataset play counts

1. Response:
    In order to farily compare the NFL model to FBS-only model, no data exclusions will be made that weren't made in the original models. The only exclusions will be: non-FBSvFBS games, non-regular season games, and plays in garbage time (>.95 or < .05 probability of winning).

    The NFL and FBS-only models performed very similarly. The cfbfastR model was calibrated very well for both, with the custom model performing well when the predicted score change was above -1. When comparing the two models, for both FBS and NFL datasets, the custom model was more conservative in predictions, leading to a more flat line. Moving on to down-to-down comparisons, we once again see very similar results. The only noticeable difference is that in the custom FBS model, Down 1 and Down 2 see more similar EP predictions by yards to endzone than in the NFL model, even overlapping at points. This appears to be due to Down 1 predictions being less than they are with the NFL dataset. EP predictions by yards to go see a different pattern, with Down 1 and Down 2 overlapping through the NFL datset, but not when using the FBS dataset, likely due to less fluctuation in the Down 1 plot.
    The primary difference came not through calibration or expected points plots, but rather by R-sq in the custom models regression results. With the NFL dataset, this was 0.209, but only a 0.125 with the FBS dataset. Even though the models formed very similar predictions with both datasets, they explain more variance within the NFL dataset than the FBS only dataset. Although we limited games to FBS only within the CFB, there is still a large skill disparity between the top and bottom teams in comparison to the NFL, likely causing such a disparity in R-sq.

----------------

2. Response:
    For this analysis, there were a few decisions made for data exclusions and model use. These exclusions included: only regular season games, no week 18 games, no garbage time, no plays within either redzone, no plays at the end of the half, no plays within overtime. These were done to attempt to eliminate plays in which the game state may influence decision making due to a disparity in the value of successfully gaining a first down, or in the case of week 18, the value of winning the game. QB kneels and spikes were explicitly taken out, as well, although they likely would already be excluded through the other filters. Weather-based filtering was considered, however, because of its variance througout the game and our inability to understand the extent of precepitation through the dataset, it was not included.
    For calculating a successful third down, I included any plays where a 1st down was gained, or when the ensuing fourth down resulted in a 1st down or score. This helps account for game states where a team may have played third down to set up a field goal or an opportunity for a fourth down conversion.
    In this model, the features included yardsToGain and Offensive team out of necessity. In addition to this, I included features of the opposing defense and if the offense is on home field to account for other important aspects of the game.
    After such filters, the model was fit on an OLS model, with the features of offensive team, defensive team, home field, and log_yardstogo. The offensive team coefficients were set so that they were relative to the league mean. This allows for easier interpretation. Alongside the full model, I made a reduced model without the offensive team features for comparison.

    Due to the p-value of the full model being extremely small (8.963e-26), it is clear that NOT all teams were equally good at making 3rd and X between 2021 and 2025. Looking at the individual teams, there were four teams that stood out positively on the models prediction of third down sucess: the Cowboys, Bills, Chiefs, and Ravens. The Cowboys were by far the best team, with a coefficient of 0.107 with the second-placed Bills at 0.053. On the other side, the Jets, Panthers, and Browns were the three worst performing teams with coefficients of -0.076, -0.051, and -0.046, respectively. Such variance in coefficients once again displays that teams are NOT all equally good at making 3rd and X.

```{python}
def process_next_score_data(df):
    # Base filtering
    filtered = df[
        (df['EP_start'].notna()) &
        (df['start.pos_team.name'].notna()) &
        # extra points not shown as their own play but rather within the td play
        (~df['orig_play_type'].isin(['Two Point Rush', 'Two Point Pass', 'Defensive 2pt Conversion'
        ]))
    ].copy()

    # Step A: Identify home scoring events
    def calc_home_score_event(row):
        if row['touchdown'] == 1:
            scoring_team = (
                row['start.pos_team.name']
                if row['offense_score_play'] == 1
                else row['start.def_pos_team.name']
            )
            if scoring_team == row['homeTeamName']:
                return 7.0
            elif scoring_team == row['awayTeamName']:
                return -7.0
        elif row['field_goal_result'] == 'made' and row['fg_team'] == row['homeTeamId']:
            return 3.0
        elif row['field_goal_result'] == 'made' and row['fg_team'] == row['awayTeamId']:
            return -3.0
        elif row['safety'] == 1 and row['start.def_pos_team.name'] == row['homeTeamName']:
            return 2.0
        elif row['safety'] == 1 and row['start.def_pos_team.name'] == row['awayTeamName']:
            return -2.0
        return np.nan

    filtered['home_scoring_event'] = filtered.apply(calc_home_score_event, axis=1)

    # Step B: Backfill within game_id and game_half
    filtered['home_scoring_event'] = (
        filtered.groupby(['game_id', 'half'])['home_scoring_event']
        .bfill()
    )

    # Step C: Fill remaining missing with 0
    filtered['home_scoring_event'] = filtered['home_scoring_event'].fillna(0)

    # Step D: Convert to possession team perspective
    filtered['pts_next_score'] = np.where(
        filtered['start.pos_team.name'] == filtered['homeTeamName'],
        filtered['home_scoring_event'],
        -filtered['home_scoring_event']
    )

    # Apply garbage time filter
    filtered = filtered[
        (filtered['wp_before'].notna()) &
        (filtered['wp_before'] >= 0.05) &
        (filtered['wp_before'] <= 0.95)
    ].copy()

    return filtered

pbp_filtered = process_next_score_data(fbs_pbp)
```

```{python}
def plot_calibration(df, bin_width=0.5, min_plays=400, title_suffix="2022-25 CFB Seasons"):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    df_copy['ep_bin'] = (df_copy['EP_start'] / bin_width).round() * bin_width

    cal_data = df_copy.groupby('ep_bin').agg(
        actual_pts=('pts_next_score', 'mean'),
        plays=('pts_next_score', 'count')
    ).reset_index()

    cal_data = cal_data[cal_data['plays'] >= min_plays]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
    sns.scatterplot(
        data=cal_data, x='ep_bin', y='actual_pts', size='plays', 
        sizes=(30, 300), color='#013369', alpha=0.7, ax=ax
    )
    ax.plot([-4, 7], [-4, 7], linestyle='--', color='#D50A0A', linewidth=2, label='Perfect Calibration')
    
    ax.set_xticks(range(-4, 8))
    ax.set_yticks(range(-4, 8))
    ax.set_title(f"Expected Points Calibration ({title_suffix})", fontweight='bold', fontsize=14)
    ax.set_xlabel("Expected Points (Binned)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Average Actual Next Score")
    ax.legend(title="Number of Plays", loc="upper left")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

plot_calibration(pbp_filtered)
```

```{python}
model_data = pbp_filtered.sort_values(['game_id', 'id']).copy()
# a few plays listed as 5th down (orig_play_type=Timeout).
#   Removed from data for feature reasons
model_data = model_data[model_data['down'].isin([1, 2, 3, 4])].copy()

# 1. Post-play scores
model_data['home_score_post'] = np.where(
    model_data['start.pos_team.name'] == model_data['homeTeamName'],
    model_data['end.pos_team_score'],
    model_data['end.def_pos_team_score']
)
model_data['away_score_post'] = np.where(
    model_data['start.pos_team.name'] == model_data['awayTeamName'],
    model_data['end.pos_team_score'],
    model_data['end.def_pos_team_score']
)

# 2. Group by game and drive
model_data = model_data[model_data['drive.id'].notna()].copy()

drive_summary = model_data.groupby(['game_id', 'drive.id']).agg(
    first_home_score=('homeScore', 'first'),
    last_home_score=('home_score_post', 'last'),
    first_away_score=('awayScore', 'first'),
    last_away_score=('away_score_post', 'last'),
    drive_posteam=('start.pos_team.name', 'first')
).reset_index()

drive_summary['drive_home_pts'] = drive_summary['last_home_score'] - drive_summary['first_home_score']
drive_summary['drive_away_pts'] = drive_summary['last_away_score'] - drive_summary['first_away_score']

model_data = model_data.merge(
    drive_summary[['game_id', 'drive.id', 'drive_home_pts', 'drive_away_pts', 'drive_posteam']], 
    on=['game_id', 'drive.id'], how='left'
)

# 3. Calculate net drive score change
model_data['drive_score_change'] = np.where(
    model_data['drive_posteam'] == model_data['homeTeamName'],
    model_data['drive_home_pts'] - model_data['drive_away_pts'],
    model_data['drive_away_pts'] - model_data['drive_home_pts']
)

# Filter missing predictors
model_data = model_data[
    model_data['down'].notna() &
    model_data['start.TimeSecsRem'].notna() &
    model_data['start.yardsToEndzone'].notna() &
    model_data['distance'].notna() &
    model_data['goal_to_go'].notna() &
    (model_data['distance'] > 0)
].copy()

model_data['log_ydstogo'] = np.log(model_data['distance'])
model_data['under_two_minutes'] = (model_data['start.TimeSecsRem'] <= 120).astype(int)
model_data['down'] = model_data['down'].astype(int).astype(str)

# Fit OLS Model
ep_model = smf.ols(
    "drive_score_change ~ C(down) + Q('start.TimeSecsRem') + Q('start.yardsToEndzone') + log_ydstogo + goal_to_go + under_two_minutes",
    data=model_data
).fit()

model_data['predicted_score_change'] = ep_model.predict(model_data)
print(ep_model.summary())
```

```{python}
def loess_smooth(x, y, frac=0.25, degree=1):
    """
    Fits a local polynomial regression (LOESS) with custom degree and span.
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    n = len(x)
    k = max(int(np.ceil(frac * n)), degree + 1)
    
    x_grid = np.linspace(x.min(), x.max(), 100)
    y_grid = np.zeros_like(x_grid)
    
    for i, xi in enumerate(x_grid):
        distances = np.abs(x - xi)
        idx = np.argsort(distances)[:k]
        
        max_dist = distances[idx[-1]]
        if max_dist == 0:
            weights = np.ones(k)
        else:
            u = distances[idx] / max_dist
            weights = np.clip((1 - u**3)**3, 0, None)
            
        w_fit = np.sqrt(weights)
        
        if np.sum(weights) == 0:
            y_grid[i] = np.mean(y[idx])
        else:
            coeffs = np.polyfit(x[idx], y[idx], deg=degree, w=w_fit)
            y_grid[i] = np.polyval(coeffs, xi)
            
    return x_grid, y_grid
```

```{python}
# 1. Prepare and aggregate field position data
plot_data = (
    model_data[model_data['down'].isin(['1', '2', '3', '4'])]
    .groupby(['down', 'start.yardsToEndzone'])
    .agg(
        cfbfastR_EP=('EP_start', 'mean'),
        Custom_Linear_EP=('predicted_score_change', 'mean'),
        plays=('EP_start', 'count')
    )
    .reset_index()
)
plot_data = plot_data[plot_data['plays'] >= 10]

# --- Parameters to customize ---
FRAC = 0.25   # Fractional window size (span)
DEGREE = 2    # 1 for linear, 2 for quadratic local fit
# -------------------------------

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), sharey=True)
models = [('Standard cfbfastR Model', 'cfbfastR_EP'), ('Custom Linear Model', 'Custom_Linear_EP')]
palette = {'1': '#e41a1c', '2': '#377eb8', '3': '#4daf4a', '4': '#984ea3'}

for ax, (model_title, ep_col) in zip(axes, models):
    for down_val in ['1', '2', '3', '4']:
        sub = plot_data[plot_data['down'] == down_val]
        
        # Apply LOESS with custom frac and degree
        x_smooth, y_smooth = loess_smooth(
            sub['start.yardsToEndzone'], sub[ep_col], frac=FRAC, degree=DEGREE
        )
        
        ax.plot(
            x_smooth, y_smooth, 
            label=f"Down {down_val}", 
            color=palette[down_val], 
            linewidth=2.5
        )
    
    ax.set_title(model_title, fontweight='bold', fontsize=12)
    ax.set_xlabel("Yards to Opponent Endzone")
    ax.set_ylabel("Expected Points (EP)" if ax == axes[0] else "")
    ax.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

axes[1].legend(title="Down", bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
fig.suptitle(f"Expected Points by Down and Field Position (frac={FRAC}, degree={DEGREE})", fontweight='bold', fontsize=14, y=1.02)

plt.show()
```

### Question 2. NFL 3rd & X


```{python}
nfl_raw = nfl.import_pbp_data([2021,2022,2023,2024,2025])
```

```{python}
# Filter out data
mask = (
    (nfl_raw['down'].isin([3, 4])) &                 # filter for 3rd & 4th downs
    (nfl_raw['season_type'] == 'REG') &              # regular season only
    (nfl_raw['week'] <= 17) &                        # no week 18
    (nfl_raw['wp'] > 0.05) & (nfl_raw['wp'] < 0.95) &     # no garbage time
    (nfl_raw['yardline_100'] > 20) &                 # non-def-red-zone
    (nfl_raw['yardline_100'] < 80) &                 # non-off-red-zone
    (nfl_raw['half_seconds_remaining'] > 30) &       # not end of half
    (nfl_raw['qtr'] <= 4) &                          # no overtime
    (nfl_raw['qb_kneel'] == 0) &
    (nfl_raw['qb_spike'] == 0) &
    nfl_raw['posteam'].notna() &
    nfl_raw['defteam'].notna() &
    nfl_raw['ydstogo'].notna()
)
nfl_pbp = nfl_raw[mask].copy()
```

```{python}
# Defining success
conv = np.where(nfl_pbp['down'] == 3, nfl_pbp['third_down_converted'], nfl_pbp['fourth_down_converted']).astype(float)
scored = nfl_pbp['drive_ended_with_score'].fillna(0).astype(float)
nfl_pbp['success'] = np.where((conv == 1) | (scored == 1), 1, 0)

# add home field feature
nfl_pbp['home_field'] = (nfl_pbp['posteam'] == nfl_pbp['home_team']).astype(int)

nfl_pbp = nfl_pbp[['success', 'ydstogo', 'posteam', 'defteam', 'home_field']].dropna()
nfl_pbp['posteam'] = nfl_pbp['posteam'].astype('category')
nfl_pbp['defteam'] = nfl_pbp['defteam'].astype('category')
nfl_pbp['log_ydstogo'] = np.log(nfl_pbp['ydstogo'])

```

```{python}
# OLS model
full = smf.ols(
    "success ~ C(posteam, Sum) + C(defteam) + home_field + log_ydstogo",
    data=nfl_pbp
).fit()

reduced = smf.ols(
    "success ~ C(defteam) + home_field + log_ydstogo",
    data=nfl_pbp
).fit()

# F-test for the posteam effect
ftest = full.compare_f_test(reduced)
print(f"F-statistic: {ftest[0]:.3f}, p-value: {ftest[1]:.3e}, df_diff: {ftest[2]}")

print(full.summary())
```

```{python}
coefs = full.params[full.params.index.str.contains('posteam')].sort_values(ascending=False)
print(coefs)
```

```{python}
# Get posteam coefficients and p-values
posteam_mask = full.params.index.str.contains(r'posteam, Sum\)')
plot_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'coef': full.params[posteam_mask],
    'pval': full.pvalues[posteam_mask]
})
plot_df.index = plot_df.index.str.extract(r'\[S\.(\w+)\]')[0].values

# Recover the omitted team
all_teams = nfl_pbp['posteam'].cat.categories
omitted_team = [t for t in all_teams if t not in plot_df.index][0]
plot_df.loc[omitted_team] = {'coef': -plot_df['coef'].sum(), 'pval': np.nan}

plot_df = plot_df.sort_values('coef', ascending=True)

# Color by significance/direction
colors = ['red' if (p < 0.05 and c < 0) else
          'green' if (p < 0.05 and c > 0) else
          'grey'
          for c, p in zip(plot_df['coef'], plot_df['pval'])]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 10))
ax.barh(plot_df.index, plot_df['coef'], color=colors)
ax.axvline(0, color='black', linewidth=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel('Offensive team coefficient (deviation from league average)')
ax.set_title('Team Offensive Effect on 3rd/4th Down Conversion')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
